feature: Feature 3 — Creating coins: the mint flow, the auto-namer, and the anti-duplicate check
summary: The create flow turns a story Insidor detected into a live pump.fun coin in two steps and one signature, with the story locked at the top so a coin can never be made out of nothing. Its one job is to make the CREATE path — the state the matcher lands in 15-30% of the time by design (D1 abstain) and 50-70% of the time by story coinability (§3.5) — a first-class monetised outcome rather than a consolation prize. The interesting half is the auto-namer, which does not ask a model to invent a ticker: it harvests the phrase people are already repeating across the cluster, ranks candidates deterministically, and uses one Haiku call only to choose and title-case among grounded spans, with a hard substring gate that makes a $KANG-class hallucination structurally impossible.
mechanism:
## A. THE AUTO-NAMER

### A0. The premise that decides the whole design
A memecoin's name is not a description of the post. It is **the phrase people are already repeating.** WIF is not "dog with hat", it is `dog wif hat` with the misspelling preserved because the misspelling is the meme. MOODENG is a proper name. SIXSEVEN and HAWKTUAH are utterances. CHILLGUY is a caption with the spaces removed. In every real case the ticker is a *span that already exists in the corpus*, not a synthesis.

That reframes the namer from a generation problem into a **retrieval + normalisation problem**, and retrieval is something Insidor is uniquely positioned to do because it holds the whole cluster, not one post. The thing that goes viral is the thing that gets quoted; the thing that gets quoted has a high `df_in_story`.

Consequence: **the model never authors a token.** It ranks and title-cases grounded spans. This is the create-path application of §5.4's rule that SUGGESTED is a prefill input and never a verdict.

### A1. Stage 0 — deterministic harvest (no model call, ~4ms, runs at PROMOTE and is cached on the story)

Six candidate sources, each carrying provenance:

| src | extraction | weight `w_source` |
|---|---|---|
| `cashtag` | `/\$([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{1,12})\b/` over `narrative_posts.text` + `sample_replies` across the whole cluster | 1.00 |
| `onscreen` | OCR of the selected video frame / image; on TikTok the on-screen caption is the meme far more often than the spoken audio | 0.85 |
| `ngram` | n=1..4 spans scored by the §3.5 distinctiveness formula generalised to n-grams | 0.80 |
| `entity` | proper nouns from the clustering call's `subject` when `subject_type ∈ {animal, character, object, place, brand, phrase}` | 0.75 |
| `mint_in_post` | a base58 mint pasted in a post → not a name candidate, it is a **duplicate signal**; routed to §B | n/a |
| `llm_prior` | existing `post_meme_scores.suggested_ticker` / `suggested_name` for posts in this story | 0.35 |

```
distinctiveness(span) = (df_in_story(span) / n_posts) × ln( N_posts_24h / (1 + df_global_24h(span)) )
```
Keep spans with `df_in_story ≥ 2`, or `df_in_story = 1` when the story has one post and the span is in the top post. `llm_prior` is **never allowed to be the primary unless at least one of cashtag/onscreen/ngram/entity corroborates it** — this is the create-path guard against the exact mechanism that produced $KANG.

### A2. Stage 1 — normalise to ticker form
```
norm(span) = upper(span) |> strip non-[A-Z0-9] |> collapse
```
- Length: hard cap **13** (`create_v2` symbol limit), target **4-9**.
- Multi-word → joined with no separator (`just a chill guy` → `JUSTACHILLGUY` 13ch → too long).
- Over-length recovery, in order: (a) drop stopwords (`JUSTACHILLGUY` → `CHILLGUY`); (b) the single most-distinctive word if it clears the generic test; (c) initials only when ≥3 words and it reads as an acronym. **Never truncate mid-word** — `CHILLG` is dead on arrival and signals low effort to every trader who sees it.
- Deliberate misspellings from the source are preserved verbatim. Never "corrected".
- Reject: `GENERIC` set (VIRAL, MEME, TREND, NEWS, TODAY, GUY, MAN, DOG, CAT, LOL alone), leading digit, and `storyDf(term,'30d') / N_stories_30d ≥ 0.02` (the §3.5 generic-subject test, reused).

### A3. Stage 2 — ranking (this is what renders instantly; the model has not been called yet)
```
score(c) = 0.34·w_source(c)
         + 0.26·min( df_in_story / max(3, 0.25·n_posts), 1 )
         + 0.18·clamp01( distinctiveness / 10 )
         + 0.12·len_fit(c)
         + 0.10·( 1 − collision_pressure(c) )

len_fit            = 1.0 (4-9ch) | 0.7 (3ch or 10-11ch) | 0.35 (12-13ch) | 0 otherwise
collision_pressure = clamp01( log10(1 + max_liquidity_usd_of_live_tokens_with_that_symbol) / 7 )
```
`collision_pressure` reuses the §5.6 `collision_idf` intuition from the other direction: a symbol already carrying a $10M token is a bad name to ship, not because of legal risk but because your coin is unfindable.

### A4. Stage 3 — one `claude-haiku-4-5` call, structured output, ~900in/250out ≈ $0.0005

**System prompt (verbatim, ~700 tokens — do not prompt-cache, Haiku's minimum cacheable prefix is 4,096):**
```
You name memecoins from viral posts.

A memecoin's name is not a description of the post. It is THE PHRASE PEOPLE ARE
ALREADY REPEATING. Find that phrase in the evidence you are given and normalise
it. Never invent one.

How real memecoins get named, in priority order:
1 CASHTAG   the post or replies already contain $TICKER. Use it. That is reading,
            not naming.
2 UTTERANCE the thing that was said, quoted verbatim, misspellings preserved.
            "hawk tuah" -> HAWKTUAH.  "six seven" -> SIXSEVEN.
3 PHRASE    the caption people repeat, spaces removed. "just a chill guy" ->
            CHILLGUY. "dog wif hat" -> WIF. Keep deliberate misspellings; the
            misspelling IS the meme.
4 ENTITY    the proper name of the animal, character, object or place.
            "Moo Deng" -> MOODENG.  "Pesto the penguin" -> PESTO.
5 NEVER a description. "hippo baby zoo thailand" is not a name. MOODENG is.

Hard rules:
- Every candidate must come from source_spans. Quote it verbatim in source_span.
  If you cannot ground a candidate in a provided span, do not produce it.
- symbol: A-Z0-9 only, starts with a letter, 3-13 chars, target 4-9.
- name: <=32 chars, the human-readable form of the SAME phrase, title case.
- Never a private individual's real name. Public figures and stage names are fine.
- Never propose a symbol in exclude_symbols.
- If collisions[symbol].max_liquidity_usd > 50000, deprioritise it: a large coin
  already owns that ticker.
- The three alternatives must differ in KIND from the primary and from each other.
  If primary is a phrase, give an utterance, an entity, and a short compression.
- If no phrase repeats and no entity is named, set namable=false and say why in one
  plain sentence a non-crypto person would understand. Do not force a name.
```

**User message:** `{story:{title, blurb, subject, subject_type, platforms, combined_views, n_posts}, posts:[top 3 by views: {platform, handle, views, text, onscreen_text, top_replies[3]}], source_spans:[{span, kind, df_in_story, distinctiveness, in_replies}] (top 12), entity_keys[8], collisions:{SYM:{n_live, max_liquidity_usd}}, exclude_symbols[], attempt}`

**Output schema:** `{namable:bool, reason_if_not:string|null, primary:{symbol,name,source_span,kind,why}, alternatives:[3 × same]}`

### A5. The hallucination gate — the load-bearing 12 lines
Server-side, before anything reaches the UI, in order. Any failure discards the **entire** model output and falls back to the Stage-3 deterministic ranking:
1. `source_span` must be a case-insensitive substring of `concat(posts[].text, onscreen_text, top_replies, entity_keys, source_spans[].span)`.
2. `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{2,12}$`
3. `len(name) ≤ 32`, `len(symbol) ≤ 13`
4. `symbol ∉ blocklist ∪ exclude_symbols`
5. `symbol == norm(source_span)` **or** `symbol` is a whole-word subset of `norm(source_span)` — blocks creative leaps while allowing stopword-dropping.
6. generic test (A2).

This is why the namer cannot produce a $KANG. A ticker that appears nowhere in the corpus cannot survive rule 1.

### A6. The render contract — the form never waits on the model
`p50` for the Haiku call is ~700-900ms; the form must open in <100ms. So:
- Form opens instantly populated with the **deterministic #1**, `.namer-why` shimmering.
- Model result arrives → if the user has touched neither field, fields swap and `.namer-why` fills. If the user has typed **anything**, the model's primary silently becomes alternative slot 1 instead. Never yank text out from under a typing user.
- Model unavailable / `_scoringPaused` / >2.5s timeout → deterministic list stands, `.namer-why` reads `Suggestions are off right now — pick a name yourself.`

### A7. Alternatives and regeneration
Three alternative `.achip`s, selected for **diversity of kind**, not next-best score: one compression, one entity/proper noun, one drawn from a *different post* in the cluster. Each carries a `--dim` micro-provenance (`in the caption`, `said in 34 posts`, `from the replies`).

`↻ Try another`:
- Presses 1-2 are **free and local** — they cycle to ranked candidates 4-8, already computed. No network, no cost, instant.
- Press 3 fires a second model call with `exclude_symbols = everything shown` and `attempt: 2`.
- Hard cap 3 model calls per user per story. After that: `That's every angle we found. Type your own.`
- **Regeneration never changes the image and never changes the story.** Only the symbol+name pair. The image is evidence; re-rolling it would sever the link to the post.
- Every run writes `namer_run{shown, accepted_symbol, accepted_edited}`. What users pick over what was ranked #1 is a free, self-growing label set for re-fitting the A3 weights. This is the same trick §5.9 applies to the buy path.

### A8. No namable subject — three distinct outcomes, never one generic error
| Cause | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `coinability_tier = 0` (identifiable private individual, death, violence against a named person, minors) — **D3** | The story never surfaces. Not a create-flow state at all. |
| `coinability_tier = 1` (public tragedy, ongoing disaster) | The Create CTA is **never rendered** on any surface. If reached by a stale link: `This story isn't available to coin.` + `Back to the story`. No mechanics explained, no "why?" link — explaining the boundary is a bypass manual. |
| `namable = false` on an otherwise normal story | **The form opens anyway.** Ticker field empty with placeholder, `.coll` in default state, and `.namer-empty` replaces the alternatives row: `We couldn't find a name in this story — no phrase repeats across the posts. Pick one yourself.` Below it, the top 5 `entity_keys` as non-committal chips labelled `words from the posts` so the user has raw material. Create enables the moment the field validates. **The namer is an accelerant, never a gate.** |

### A9. The image — decision: the source post's media, cropped, re-hosted. Never generated.

Four reasons, in order of weight:
1. **It is the evidence.** The thesis is that the coin is downstream of the story. A generated logo severs the visual link that makes the coin recognisable to the next 10,000 people who watch the same video. Recognition is distribution.
2. **Insidor's own matcher depends on it.** §5.8 gives `S_img = 1.00` at `hamming(pHash) ≤ 6`. A crop of the post's media confirms against the post at ~1.0. A generated logo lands in the SigLIP channel, **capped at 0.60, which cannot confirm alone** — meaning Insidor would mint coins its own pipeline cannot verify. Disqualifying.
3. **§3.16 measured 58.6% byte-identical duplicate logos** across the newest 599 pump.fun coins. Generating puts us in that bucket, indistinguishable from slop.
4. Generation adds 5-15s to a flow whose pitch is "30 seconds" inside a 20-90 minute head start.

**Production pipeline:**
- `media_type = photo` → center-weighted square crop, 1000×1000, PNG q90, ≤2MB.
- `media_type = video` → **frame selection, not frame 0.** Frame 0 on TikTok is usually black or a title card. Sample 5 frames at 10/25/40/55/70% of duration; pick max Laplacian variance (sharpness) among frames with the largest subject bbox; tie-break earliest. If OCR found on-screen text, prefer a frame where the text is legible — the text *is* the meme. `ffmpeg` server-side, ~600ms.
- `media_type = link` → the OG image of the linked page.
- **No media (text-only X post)** → render the post itself: text set in Clash Display on `#0C0C0E`, platform mark, handle, 1000×1000. This is not generating art, it is a screenshot of the evidence — which is what people screenshot anyway. Deterministic, on-brand, still pHash-matchable to the post record.
- Every image is SHA-256'd and **re-hosted to Insidor storage** before upload (gotcha 33: 43% of logo URLs point at `ipfs.io`; the hash also feeds the anti-dupe index and the IDF penalty for free).
- User may upload their own (PNG/JPG/GIF ≤2MB). If they do, a persistent `--dim` line: `Custom image — this won't match the post automatically.` Because it measurably degrades the story→coin match and they should know.

**Crop UI:** 1:1 frame over the media, drag to reposition, zoom slider. Two presets `Fit` (letterbox onto `#060607`) / `Fill` (center crop); default `Fill`. No filters, no text tools, no stickers.

---

## B. THE ANTI-DUPLICATE CHECK

Search's entire reason to exist, executed inside the create flow. Runs three times: **on open**, **debounced 250ms per keystroke ≥2ch**, and **again immediately before signing** with a 6s timeout — because ~40 seconds elapse between open and sign and that is precisely the window in which someone else mints.

### B1. Corpora and queries
```sql
-- 1. exact + near symbol.  LIQUIDITY-first, never volume-first (§5.1 correction).
select mint, symbol, name, image_sha256, first_mint_at, liquidity_usd, mcap_usd, holders
from   coin_index
where  symbol_norm = $1 or symbol_norm % $1          -- pg_trgm, sim >= 0.6
order  by liquidity_usd desc nulls last, first_mint_at asc
limit  20;

-- 2. image duplicate (only while the image is still the post's media)
select mint, symbol, first_mint_at, liquidity_usd,
       bit_count(image_phash # $phash) as dist
from   coin_index
where  bit_count(image_phash # $phash) <= 6
  and  first_mint_at > now() - interval '7 days'
order  by dist asc limit 10;

-- 3. this story's own matches (already computed by §5)
select ticker, mint_ca, match_state, match_score, liquidity, mcap, first_deployed
from   narrative_tickers
where  narrative_id = $story and match_state in ('CONFIRMED','UNSURE');
```
Live overlay: Jupiter `tokens/v2/search?query={symbol}` for anything the index has stale, because `coin_index` freshness is the failure mode that matters here.

### B2. The push ladder — four bands, four different pressures
| Band | Trigger | How hard we push |
|---|---|---|
| **D-CONFIRMED** | `narrative_tickers.match_state='CONFIRMED'` for *this* story | **The form does not open.** THE ONE RULE: the entry point renders `Buy $TICKER` instead. If a coin lands mid-session with the form already open, the sheet swaps to a full interstitial: `$FERRY was made 40 seconds ago.` → `Buy $FERRY` primary, `Make a different one` as a text link. Framed as a save, not a loss. |
| **D-STRONG** | exact symbol **and** `first_mint_at ≥ earliest_post_at − 10min` **and** `liquidity ≥ $1k` **and** (pHash ≤ 6 **or** name-cos ≥ 0.75) | Strongest push short of blocking. `.coll.taken` expands into a `.dupe-card` (icon, symbol, name, money in it, owners, age, `made 4m after the post`). **Primary button becomes `Buy $FERRY`**; `Create it anyway` demotes to a bordered secondary requiring one extra tap, and the cost line gains `You'd be the second $FERRY. The first has $18.2K in it.` We never fully block — a competing coin is a legitimate intent, and D1 says show the uncertainty, not hide the option. |
| **D-WEAK** | exact symbol but >48h older than the story, **or** zero liquidity, **or** a different subject — the $KANG/$PUMP class | **Informational only.** One amber line: `$PUMP already exists — a $1.8B token from 2024, unrelated to this story. Yours would be a different coin with the same ticker.` **Primary stays `Create $PUMP`.** Pushing a user toward a 2024 major off a fresh story is exactly the bug §5 exists to kill; the anti-dupe check must not reintroduce it from the other direction. |
| **D-IMAGE** | pHash ≤ 6 against a mint in the last 7 days, symbol differs | Amber line + `.dupe-card`: `This image is already a coin — $CUPS, made 12m ago, $4.1K in it.` Secondary `See $CUPS`. **Primary stays Create** — same image under a different ticker is a real fork, not a duplicate. |

### B3. Interaction with the UNSURE band (the subtle part)
Per §5.9 an UNSURE story's CTA is already `Create the coin`, so the create form is the *correct* destination, not a mistake to be corrected.

- The UNSURE candidate renders **once**, in a `.dupe-unsure` block **above** the name grid — not in `.coll`. Muted `--dim` border, no amber: `Possibly already made: $KANG — we're not confident it's from this story. [View it]`.
- **An UNSURE match never demotes the create button and never changes the primary.** Two reasons: (a) D1 — abstain never means hide, and it equally never means *push*; applying amber pressure on a 0.45-0.79 score converts an honest abstention into a recommendation. (b) Security — score-gated suppression is a denial-of-creation vector: mint a decoy with a matching ticker and you suppress everyone else's create flow on a hot story.
- The push ladder is therefore gated on `match_state='CONFIRMED'` **or** on hard independent evidence (exact symbol + temporal window + image-or-name), **never on `match_score` alone.**
- If the proposed ticker happens to equal the UNSURE symbol: one line under the field, `Same ticker as the possible match above.` Nothing more.
- The namer **excludes** the UNSURE symbol from `primary` but keeps it as alternative #1, labelled `possible match`. The user can still choose it deliberately.

### B4. Degradation
- `coin_index` freshness > 3 min → `.coll` gains `--dim` line `Checking against coins up to 4 minutes old.` and the pre-sign re-check bypasses the index entirely, going direct to Jupiter/DexScreener.
- Pre-sign re-check times out or errors → **does not block signing.** `Couldn't re-check for duplicates` in the confirm panel, user may proceed. A failed read must never consume the user's head start.

---

## C. TRANSACTION MECHANICS

### C1. What is signed
```ts
const mint = Keypair.generate();                    // persisted before signing (see F4)
ix1 = PUMP_SDK.createV2Instruction({
  mint: mint.publicKey,
  name,                    // <= 32
  symbol,                  // <= 13
  uri,                     // <= 200, ipfs://...
  creator: creatorPubkey,  // independent of `user` — officially sanctioned
  user: signerPubkey,
});
ix2 = firstBuyLamports > 0 ? PUMP_SDK.buyInstruction({...}) : null;   // BUNDLED
ix3 = D2 ? PUMP_FEES.createFeeSharingConfig({...}) : null;            // config only, no shares
// tx2, deferred: PUMP_FEES.updateFeeSharesV2([...]) after poster address verification
```
- **The first buy is bundled into the launch tx.** Two signatures for one action is worse UX, and an unbundled dev buy is strictly worse than everyone else's — the sniper bots win the gap. Failure of the buy fails the launch, and the confirm screen says so: `If your first buy can't fill, the whole launch is cancelled and nothing is spent.` (In practice it always fills — you are the first buyer at the curve floor.)
- **`creator` may differ from `user`.** Today they are the same. The moment they diverge, the confirm screen must show **two rows** — `Signed by` and `Creator on-chain` — because a silent divergence is a footgun aimed at the user.
- **Shares are deferred, config is not** (§3.2): `createFeeSharingConfig` is not the locking call; `updateFeeSharesV2` is. Creating the config at launch and writing shares seconds later, after the poster's derived address is verified, is materially safer than one blind transaction. Cost: any trade in the gap pays 100% to the creator — which we disclose rather than hide.

### C2. Cost, itemised (shown in a popover on the cost label)
```
Mint + metadata rent          ~0.0155 SOL     Token-2022 mint, bonding curve, metadata
pump.fun creation fee          0.0000 SOL     creation itself is free
Network fee (priority incl.)  ~0.0006 SOL
Fee-sharing config            ~0.0043 SOL     only when the split ships
Your first buy                 0.0000 SOL
──────────────────────────────────────────
Total                         ~0.0204 SOL  ≈  $4.02
```
**FLAG:** exact rent is research item U2 — unverified. Until a devnet `create_v2` is measured, the UI shows `~0.02 SOL` with `about`, never a precise figure, and the balance gate requires **0.03 SOL** so we never quote a number the transaction then exceeds. The poster's 890,880-lamport account rent (U1 mitigation) is paid by **Insidor's platform wallet in tx 2**, not by the creator — making a creator fund a stranger's account is indefensible and it never appears in their cost line.

### C3. Retry safety
`launch.mint_keypair` is persisted (encrypted, server-side) **before** the first signature. Any retry after a possible-landing reuses the **same mint keypair**, so if the original transaction confirms late the retry fails deterministically with `account already in use` rather than producing two coins. Never issue a retry that generates a fresh mint while an earlier signature is unresolved.

---

## D. PROPAGATION — how the new coin reaches the boards and attaches to its story
| Surface | Mechanism | Latency |
|---|---|---|
| Story's coin list | `insert into narrative_tickers(narrative_id, ticker, mint_ca, source='insidor_launch', match_state='CONFIRMED', match_score=1.0, first_deployed=now())` — **written by our own server, bypassing the matcher**, because we have ground truth: we minted it from this story | optimistic, immediate |
| Story primary CTA everywhere | derived from `count(match_state='CONFIRMED')` flipping 0→1 → every viewer's button becomes `Buy $CHILLGUY` | Supabase Realtime on `narrative_tickers`, <1s |
| Tokens / New Pairs tables | `liveRow()` with `justDeployed=true`, `.newbadge NEW`; **all nine numeric cells render `—`, never `0`** (§5.3: missing data fails closed) | optimistic; real data on next Jupiter/DexScreener poll |
| Live rail → Launches | `launchCard()` prepend with `.tape-tag NEW` | Realtime |
| Live rail → Viral | unchanged — creating a coin is not a viral event |
| Creator's You → Launches | `launch` row | immediate |
| Follow | **two** rows: auto-follow the coin *and* keep the story follow (flow-doc FIX: following a story never silently becomes following a coin) | immediate |
| Search / anti-dupe | synchronous insert into `coin_index` with `is_insidor_launch=true`, so the *next* user's duplicate check catches it within seconds rather than on the next indexer tick | <2s |

**Brand-new-token state (first ~60-90s):** no DexScreener pair, no Jupiter price. `.qstats` all `—`, chart shows `.chart-empty` `No live SOL pair for this token yet`, trade box quote disabled with `price appears once there's a pair`, age reads `just now`.

screens.job: Offer Create in exactly the places where CONFIRMED coin count is zero, carrying enough context that the form never has to ask the user what they meant.
screens.layout: Not a page — seven existing components across five surfaces. Every one reads a single server-derived boolean `story.can_create` and a single integer `confirmed_count`. No client-side coinability logic exists anywhere.

elements.element: E1 · Story page footer primary — existing `.deploy-go` inside `.sh-foot.nm-foot-buy` (component inventory §7.4)
elements.shows: Label `Create coin` when `confirmed_count = 0`; `Buy $TICKER` at 1; `See the 3 coins` at ≥2
elements.source: count(narrative_tickers where narrative_id=$ and match_state='CONFIRMED') · narratives.can_create
elements.interaction: Opens the create sheet with `{narrative_id, top_post_id, entry:'story_primary'}`. The canonical path — full namer, full split.

elements.element: E2 · Narrative table row, cell 5 — existing `.btn-deploy-mini.deploy-narr` (`data-deploy-narr`, §4.3 cell 5)
elements.shows: Pill labelled `Create` in place of the market-cap number
elements.source: narrative_tickers rollup; renders the cap instead when a CONFIRMED coin has liquidity>0 and mcap>0
elements.interaction: Same payload + `entry:'narr_row'`. Identical form — a shortcut, not a variant.

elements.element: E3 · Story page with an UNSURE match — same `.deploy-go`, label unchanged
elements.shows: `Create the coin` (§5.9: UNSURE never renders Buy)
elements.interaction: Payload adds `unsure_candidates:[{mint,symbol,score}]`. Form renders `.dupe-unsure` above the name grid; primary button unaffected.

elements.element: E4 · Viral rail card / post row — existing `.pbtn.deploy` in `.note-acts` (`data-deploy-post`, §6.8)
elements.shows: `Create Coin`
elements.interaction: `.src-quote` shows THIS post, not the story's top post — the user pointed at a specific one. Image sources from this post's media; the namer weights this post 2× in the n-gram harvest.

elements.element: E4b · Post row on a post with no narrative yet (below PROMOTE)
elements.shows: Same button
elements.interaction: The only path where a coin originates from a post. On submit the server creates a single-post narrative with `source='user_created'` so the invariant `every coin has a story` holds. FLAGGED as a decision — see openQuestions.

elements.shows: The dead end converted into an action

elements.element: E7 · Coin page side rail — `Make your own coin`
elements.shows: Secondary action under an existing coin's page
elements.interaction: The deliberate second coin. Form opens with the D-STRONG panel pre-expanded showing the existing coin, and the namer excludes every existing symbol from all candidates. `.coll` reads `$CHILLGUY exists — yours would be a different coin.`

states: can_create=true, confirmed=0 → Create CTA
confirmed=1 → Buy $TICKER, no Create at primary (E7 secondary only)
confirmed>=2 → See the N coins, no Create at primary
unsure>=1, confirmed=0 → Create the coin (unchanged label)
coinability_tier=1 (public tragedy) → no CTA rendered anywhere, story still visible and discussable
coinability_tier=0 → story never surfaces at all
story data stale (updated_at > 10 min) → CTA still active; creation does not require a live pipeline
wallet not connected → CTA still active; connection is deferred to the sign step

Body `.sh-body` scrolls, `max-height: min(72vh, calc(100dvh - 200px))`, eight stacked blocks, gap 15px. Footer `.sh-foot` pinned: cost on the left, primary on the right.

dataContract:
## Exists today and is used as-is
- `narratives.{id, title, blurb, img_seed, platforms, combined_views, lead_time_min, lifecycle, display_eligible, gate_reason, trend_term, updated_at, first_seen_at, created_at, top_post_id}`
- `narrative_posts.{id, narrative_id, platform, platform_post_id, handle, text, media_url, media_type, image, views, likes, retweets, quotes, replies, sample_replies, posted_at, first_seen_at}` — `sample_replies` is a first-class namer input (replies are where a phrase proves it is being repeated); `(platform, platform_post_id)` already unique-indexed.
- `narrative_tickers.{id, narrative_id, ticker, name, mint_ca, liquidity, mcap, holders, vol24h, age_min, first_deployed, canonical, safety, smart_money}`
- `post_meme_scores.{post_id, suggested_ticker, suggested_name, meme_score, reason}` — **the create form is the ONLY sanctioned consumer of `suggested_*`** (§5.4: SUGGESTED is a create-path prefill, never a resolution input). Ranked last, weight 0.35, and it can never be primary without corroboration.
- `post_embeddings.embedding` — reused for the name-similarity leg of the anti-dupe check.

## DOES NOT EXIST — blocking, in dependency order

### 1. Columns on existing tables
| Column | Why the create flow needs it |
|---|---|
| `narratives.promoted_at timestamptz` | **The success screen's central sentence** (`made 4 minutes after we spotted it`) and `launch.minutes_after_promote` are both arithmetic on it. §1 says it is set once, forever. Backfill `coalesce(first_seen_at, created_at)` exactly once, then make it immutable at the DB level. |
| `narratives.coinability_tier smallint` (0/1/2) + `coinable boolean` + `sensitive boolean` | **D3 enforcement.** Every Create CTA reads one derived boolean. Without this the tier-1 suppression is client-side, i.e. not enforcement. |
| `narratives.subject text` + `subject_type text` | Namer input (`entity` source), §3.5 output with nowhere to live today. |
| `narratives.entity_keys text[]` | The distinctiveness pre-pass output — the namer's raw material and the `words from the posts` chips in the `namable=false` state. |
| `narratives.title_centroid vector` + `titled_at timestamptz` | §3.5 anti-churn regeneration policy; the create form must not open on a story whose title changed 4 seconds ago. |
| `narrative_tickers.source text` | `'cashtag' \| 'llm' \| 'mint_in_post' \| 'insidor_launch'`. **Blocking**: the propagation step writes `source='insidor_launch'`, and §5.4 makes provenance non-optional. |
| `narrative_tickers.match_state text` + `match_score numeric` + `match_features jsonb` | §5.7's CONFIRMED/UNSURE/REJECTED/ADOPTED verdict has nowhere to live. Every entry-point CTA and the whole B2 push ladder are functions of `match_state`. |
| `narrative_posts.ocr_text text` | On-screen text is the highest-yield namer source on TikTok and does not exist anywhere today. |
| `narrative_posts.media_sha256 text` + `media_phash bit(64)` + `media_local_url text` | Gotcha 33: re-host by SHA-256. Feeds the image pipeline, the D-IMAGE duplicate band, and the story→coin `S_img` channel. |

### 2. New tables
```sql
create table launch (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  mint text unique not null,
  narrative_id uuid not null references narratives(id),   -- NOT NULL: no coin without a story
  source_post_id uuid references narrative_posts(id),     -- the post the image came from
  creator_user_id uuid not null references app_user(id),
  signer_wallet text not null,
  creator_pubkey text not null,          -- may differ from signer (create_v2)
  symbol text not null check (symbol ~ '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{2,12}$'),
  name text not null check (char_length(name) <= 32),
  metadata_uri text not null check (char_length(metadata_uri) <= 200),
  image_sha256 text not null,
  image_source text not null,   -- post_media|video_frame|og_image|rendered_text|user_upload
  image_frame_ms int,
  namer_run_id uuid references namer_run(id),
  ticker_source text not null,  -- cashtag|onscreen|ngram|entity|llm|user_typed
  first_buy_lamports bigint not null default 0,
  create_signature text,
  create_slot bigint,
  landed_at timestamptz,
  promoted_at_snapshot timestamptz,   -- narratives.promoted_at frozen here
  minutes_after_promote int,          -- frozen; can be large, never recomputed
  status text not null,               -- drafting|signing|sent|landed|failed|expired
  failure_code text,
  mint_keypair_enc bytea not null,    -- persisted BEFORE first signature; retry safety
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table namer_run (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  narrative_id uuid not null references narratives(id),
  user_id uuid references app_user(id),
  model text,                    -- claude-haiku-4-5 | deterministic | none
  attempt int not null default 1,
  candidates jsonb not null,     -- [{symbol,name,kind,source_span,df_in_story,score,collisions}]
  primary_symbol text,
  namable boolean not null,
  reason_if_not text,
  gate_failure text,             -- hallucinated_span|regex|length|blocklist|not_derivable|generic
  latency_ms int, cost_usd numeric,
  shown jsonb,                   -- exactly what the user saw
  accepted_symbol text,          -- null until submit
  accepted_edited boolean,       -- did they type over it
  created_at timestamptz default now()
);

create table fee_share (
  mint text primary key references launch(mint),
  config_pubkey text,
  shares jsonb not null,         -- [{pubkey,bps,role:'maker'|'poster'|'insidor'}]
  bps_total int not null check (bps_total = 10000),
  config_signature text, shares_signature text, shares_written_at timestamptz,
  poster_id uuid references poster(id),
  poster_derived_wallet text,
  poster_prefunded_lamports bigint,   -- U1 mitigation, 890880, paid by Insidor
  attempts int default 0, last_error text,
  status text                     -- config_created|shares_pending|shares_written|abandoned
);

create table coin_index (        -- F3.2 indexer; the ONLY anti-dupe corpus
  mint text primary key,
  symbol text, name text, symbol_norm text,
  metadata_uri text, image_url text, image_sha256 text, image_phash bit(64),
  image_dino vector(768), name_embedding vector(1024),
  first_mint_at timestamptz not null,   -- from the create_v2 slot, NOT pairCreatedAt
  creator_pubkey text,
  liquidity_usd numeric, mcap_usd numeric, holders int, last_market_at timestamptz,
  is_insidor_launch boolean default false
);
create index on coin_index (symbol_norm);
create index on coin_index using gin (symbol_norm gin_trgm_ops);
create index on coin_index (first_mint_at desc);
```
Plus `app_user`, `poster` (with `derived_wallet`, `opted_out`), `follow` and `holding` from the DESIGN.md plan — all still `❌ new`.

## Query shapes used at runtime
- **Entry-point gating** (one query, cached on the story row): `select can_create, confirmed_count, unsure_count from story_cta_v where id = $1` — a view over `narratives.coinability_tier` + the `narrative_tickers.match_state` rollup. Every CTA in the product reads this and nothing else.
- **Name candidates**: `GET /api/story/:id/name-candidates` → `{candidates[], entity_keys[], collisions{}, namable, image:{url,source,frames[]}}`. Precomputed at PROMOTE and cached; the model leg is fired on form open, not at PROMOTE (attempt-1 result is cached on the story for 20 min).
- **Anti-dupe**: the three queries in the mechanism §B1, plus a Jupiter `tokens/v2/search` overlay. Symbol query orders by **liquidity desc, then first_mint_at asc** — never by 24h volume (§5.1: volume-first ranking is what selects the $1.8B major for a fresh story).
- **Propagation write** (single transaction): insert `launch`, insert `narrative_tickers` with `source='insidor_launch', match_state='CONFIRMED', match_score=1.0`, insert `coin_index` with `is_insidor_launch=true`, insert two `follow` rows (story + coin), insert `holding` when `first_buy_lamports > 0` with `minutes_early = launch.minutes_after_promote`.

## Non-DB gaps
- **The F3.2 indexer itself.** `coin_index` has no producer today. The anti-dupe check is the create flow's most important safety feature and it is entirely downstream of an indexer that does not exist. Ship the check read-only against Jupiter search first, and treat pHash/DINO duplicate detection as phase 2.
- **OCR** for on-screen text — no service, no column, no worker.
- **ffmpeg frame extraction** service for video thumbnail selection.
- **Rendered-text image generator** (the no-media fallback).
- **Share-card renderer** and the public `/c/{mint}` OG route.
- **`getSignatureStatuses` polling endpoint** for the unconfirmed-transaction state.
- **`/api/launch/{prepare,sign,confirm,retry-shares}`** — none exist. The current `deployFiled()` fabricates a base58 string with `genCA()` and mutates a module-scope array (interaction model §6 item 2).
buildOrder: 1 · Migration 001 — the columns everything else reads: `narratives.promoted_at` (backfilled once from `coalesce(first_seen_at, created_at)`, then immutable), `coinability_tier`, `subject`, `subject_type`, `entity_keys`; `narrative_tickers.source`, `match_state`, `match_score`. Ships alone, changes no UI. Nothing downstream is buildable without it.

2 · `story_cta_v` view + `can_create` gating on every existing Create affordance (`.deploy-go`, `.btn-deploy-mini.deploy-narr`, `.pbtn.deploy`, `.deploybtn`). Tier<=1 renders no CTA anywhere, enforced server-side. This is the D3 safety floor and it ships before any new create UI exists.

3 · Deterministic candidate harvester — cashtag + n-gram distinctiveness + entity_keys + llm_prior, the A3 ranking formula, exposed at `GET /api/story/:id/name-candidates`. Wire it into the EXISTING create sheet by replacing `deriveTicker()`. Immediately better naming with zero model spend and zero new UI.

4 · Image pipeline — fetch post media, SHA-256, re-host, square crop, ffmpeg frame selection, rendered-text fallback. Adds `narrative_posts.media_sha256/media_phash/media_local_url`. Also fixes the loremflickr/picsum placeholder hack across the whole app (interaction model §6 item 11).

5 · The Haiku namer + `namer_run` table + the A5 hallucination gate + the A6 never-wait-on-model render contract. Feature-flagged; the deterministic path from step 3 is the permanent fallback, not a stub.

6 · `coin_index` + the anti-dupe check, read-only. Phase 6a: Jupiter `tokens/v2/search` only, symbol exact + trgm, liquidity-ordered — this alone delivers three of the four B2 bands. Phase 6b: the create_v2 mint stream populating `coin_index`. Phase 6c: pHash for D-IMAGE.

7 · Create Step 1, wallet-optional, terminating at `Review`. No signing, no chain. Reuses `.sheet`, `.src-quote`, `.name-grid`, `.coll`, `.achip`, `.buychips`, `.sh-foot`; adds `.namer`, `.dupe-card`, `.safety-defaults`, `.src-lock`. Shippable to internal users as a naming tool.

8 · Real launch — IPFS upload with Pinata fallback, `createV2Instruction`, bundled first buy, Privy raw-byte signing, send + confirm, `launch` table, `mint_keypair_enc` retry safety, and the complete failure taxonomy with its copy. Step 2 + Signing screens.

9 · Propagation — the single-transaction write of `narrative_tickers` (source='insidor_launch', CONFIRMED), `coin_index`, both `follow` rows, `holding`; Realtime broadcast; optimistic rows in every table with `—` not `0` for absent market data.
10 · Success screen + `/c/{mint}` OG route + share-card renderer + the X compose intent (never an auto-post).

11 · Fee split, gated on D2 — `poster` table with the opt-out registry, `fee_share` table, `createFeeSharingConfig` in tx 1, deferred `updateFeeSharesV2` in tx 2 after address verification, the retry worker with a 24h ceiling, and the `not created or endorsed by` disclaimer. All in ONE release per the risk register. Insidor's platform wallet pays the 890,880-lamport poster prefund.

12 · Regeneration UX (2 free local cycles, then attempt 2, cap 3) plus the `accepted_symbol` / `accepted_edited` label loop feeding a refit of the A3 weights. This is the only step that makes the namer improve rather than merely exist.
openQuestions: D2 is still open and it gates step 11 permanently. A coin minted without a fee-sharing config can NEVER have one added (errors 6009/6024; `reset_fee_sharing_config` is gated on a pump-held authority Insidor does not control). Every coin launched before the decision is permanently split-less. Recommendation: create the sharing config on EVERY launch from day one even while shares stay unwritten — `isSharingConfigEditable` returns true for a v2 config with no shares, so this costs ~0.0043 SOL per launch and preserves the option. Deciding 'no' later costs nothing; deciding 'yes' later is impossible.

Dev buy: the flow doc explicitly CUT 'buying your own coin ahead of everyone inside the create form' as the one screen that makes a beginner correctly ask whether they are running a scam, but the brief specifies an optional dev buy. This spec keeps it, defaults it to None, relabels it `Buy some yourself (optional)`, and states plainly that it executes at the same price in the same transaction. Confirm that middle is acceptable, or cut it entirely.

E6 (search empty state, no story): the flow doc says the form is only reachable from a story, 'which is what keeps creation coherent — but it also means you cannot make a coin about something we missed.' This spec recommends blocking storyless creation in v1 and offering `follow this search` instead. That forecloses a real user intent. Confirm.

E4b (orphan post below PROMOTE): allowing it means synthesising a single-post narrative with `source='user_created'` at submit time, which puts user-authored rows into the same table the detection pipeline owns. The alternative is refusing to coin anything we have not promoted, which loses the fastest possible launches. Which invariant matters more?

The pre-sign re-check window: a 6s timeout that does not block means a determined race still slips through. Tightening it to blocking-with-a-3s-timeout trades a rare duplicate for a common stall. Current recommendation is non-blocking; verify against real p95 latency once `coin_index` exists.

D-STRONG demotes the create button to a secondary. That is the only place in the product where Insidor steers a user toward buying rather than creating, and creating is the more monetisable outcome for us. Confirm the incentive conflict is being resolved in the user's favour deliberately, and consider logging the create-anyway rate as an honesty metric.

U2 is unresolved: the exact all-in cost of one `create_v2` (Token-2022 mint and `mayhem_state` byte sizes unverified). Until one devnet launch is measured, the cost line must read `about 0.02 SOL` and the balance gate must require 0.03. Run the devnet launch before writing the cost copy.

U1 is unresolved: whether `distribute_creator_fees_v2` throws 6070 for a zero-lamport poster account. If it does, every launch under variant A carries an 890,880-lamport prefund. This spec assigns that cost to Insidor, not the creator — confirm.

Regeneration cap of 3 model calls per user per story is a cost guess, not a measured one. At $0.0005/call it is not the money that matters, it is the slot-machine dynamic. Watch `accepted_edited` rate: if it climbs above ~40% the namer is not good enough and the cap is masking it.

Does an UNSURE match ever justify pushing toward buy? This spec says never, on both D1 grounds and denial-of-creation-attack grounds. That means we will occasionally let a user mint a second coin when the first one really was the right match. Accept that cost explicitly.

Naming a public figure: the prompt permits public figures and stage names and forbids private individuals, but the boundary is genuinely fuzzy for a person who went viral once and is otherwise private — which is the modal Insidor story. This needs a written rule from the founder, not a model judgement, and it is the D3 tier-1 edge that will actually bite.
priorArt: pump.fun's own create form — the direct baseline and the thing users will compare against. It asks for name, ticker, description, image and socials with zero assistance and no duplicate check whatsoever; the entire Insidor advantage here is that it opens pre-filled from evidence. Study its field order and its cost disclosure, then beat it on the two things it does not do.

Believe / Launchcoin (tweet-to-token) — the closest existing product to launch-from-a-post, including creator-fee attribution to a poster who did not sign up. Study specifically how it handles a poster who never claims, and how it words that to the creator, since that is exactly the variant-A disclosure problem.

Zora's 'create from post' and Farcaster's clanker — both mint from a social object and both had to solve the auto-namer. Worth reading for their failure modes: clanker in particular demonstrates what happens when the naming step is a free-text LLM with no grounding gate.

Jupiter Studio's DBC launch flow — the alternative venue named in decision D5. Its create UI is the most disclosure-heavy in Solana launch tooling and is a useful reference for the irreversibility list, even though graduating into Meteora rather than pump.fun is a positioning problem for a pump.fun-detection pipeline.

Coinbase / Robinhood first-time-crypto confirmation screens — for the confirm step specifically. The pattern worth stealing is the plain-text loss sentence that is never a dismissible red box, which the flow doc has already independently arrived at for the buy sheet.

Namecheap / domain-registrar 'that name is taken, here are alternatives' flows — the closest well-solved analogue to the anti-duplicate ladder. They have spent twenty years learning exactly how hard to push a user toward an available alternative versus the taken one, and the four-band structure here is directly borrowed from that lineage.
